name: UUIDv7 / ULID Primary Keys
when_to_use: Distributed systems, APIs exposing IDs to clients, multi-tenant databases, systems needing time-sortable IDs
avoid_when: Small single-node internal lookup tables with no public exposure
rules_and_spec: Use UUIDv7 (RFC 9562) or ULID. Store as 16-byte UUID in Postgres/MySQL. B-tree index friendly.
trade_offs: 16 bytes storage vs 8-byte BigInt; eliminates central auto-increment sequence bottleneck
anti_patterns: Random UUIDv4 as clustered PK (causes massive B-tree page splits and index fragmentation)

name: BigInt Auto-Increment Primary Keys
when_to_use: Internal relational tables, audit logs, strictly private tables with low distributed concurrency
avoid_when: Public APIs where sequential IDs expose business volume or invite enumeration attacks
rules_and_spec: Use BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (SQL standard). Fits naturally in 8 bytes.
trade_offs: 8 bytes compact storage vs distributed sequence collision and enumeration vulnerability
anti_patterns: INT (32-bit) which overflows at 2.1 billion rows; exposing auto-increment IDs in public URLs

name: 3NF Relational Normalization
when_to_use: Core OLTP transactional entities (billing, orders, accounts, identity, inventory)
avoid_when: Analytical data warehouses (OLAP), append-only time-series metric aggregates
rules_and_spec: Eliminate transitive and partial dependencies; each non-key column depends on the whole key and nothing but the key.
trade_offs: Guarantees consistency and eliminates update anomalies vs requires JOINs for complex queries
anti_patterns: Using JSONB/document columns as an escape hatch to avoid modeling structured relational entities

name: Plain String Enum Storage
when_to_use: Application-domain statuses and workflow states in ORM-backed services (e.g. OrderStatus, PaymentState)
avoid_when: Truly static physical constants that will never change (e.g. DaysOfWeek, CompassDirection)
rules_and_spec: Store as VARCHAR/TEXT with application-level validation and selective CHECK invariants if static.
trade_offs: Avoids PostgreSQL ALTER TYPE exclusive locks during rolling zero-downtime deployments
anti_patterns: Native PostgreSQL CREATE TYPE enum which requires exclusive catalog locks and complicates rollback

name: Invariant CHECK Constraints
when_to_use: Stable, invariant physical domain rules (e.g. amount >= 0, end_date >= start_date, percentage BETWEEN 0 AND 100)
avoid_when: Frequently changing business rules, mutable workflow state machines, application status lists
rules_and_spec: Enforce physical integrity at DB engine level: CHECK (price_cents >= 0), CHECK (starts_at <= ends_at)
trade_offs: Prevents corrupt invalid data from entering DB vs requires migration to alter rule
anti_patterns: Enforcing volatile application business workflows inside DB check constraints instead of app layer

name: Optimistic Concurrency Control
when_to_use: Entities subject to concurrent user updates with read-modify-write cycles (e.g. bank balances, inventory, drafts)
avoid_when: Append-only tables, write-once immutable event logs, pure read workloads
rules_and_spec: Add version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1. UPDATE table SET col = val, version = version + 1 WHERE id = x AND version = old_version.
trade_offs: No database lock holding during user think-time vs requires retry on optimistic concurrency conflict
anti_patterns: Pessimistic SELECT FOR UPDATE held open across long-running HTTP transactions

name: Append-Only Audit Log Tables
when_to_use: Financial transactions, healthcare records, security permissions, regulatory change tracking
avoid_when: Ephemeral caches, high-frequency telemetry metrics where point-in-time state is irrelevant
rules_and_spec: Separate audit table (id, entity_id, entity_type, action, changed_by, old_state, new_state, created_at). Write atomically with mutation.
trade_offs: Full immutable historical audit trail vs extra storage and write overhead
anti_patterns: Naive in-place updates overwriting critical financial/security history with no record of who changed it

name: Soft Deletion with Partial Index
when_to_use: Entities requiring user-facing trash/undo, regulatory retention before hard purge
avoid_when: High-frequency ephemeral rows, many-to-many relationship join tables
rules_and_spec: Add deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL. MUST create partial unique indexes: UNIQUE(email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.
trade_offs: Safe recovery vs query complexity (every query needs WHERE deleted_at IS NULL without partial index)
anti_patterns: Naive boolean is_deleted flag without partial index, breaking standard UNIQUE constraints
